attacker_control.reason: The id value comes from the query string of an HTTP request.

privilege_boundary.reason: Any logged-in user can read rows of other users through the query.

unmitigated.reason: The value is formatted into SQL text without binding or validation.

finding.title: SQL injection in user lookup
finding.description: GET /users formats the id parameter into a SQL statement.
finding.root_cause: find_user builds SQL with an f-string.
finding.intended_behavior: The query must bind user_id as a parameter.

trace.description: Reads id from the query string.

evidence.description: The f-string puts user_id into the SQL text.

conditions.description: The attacker needs any user account.

execution.attacker_perspective: A logged-in user with a normal account.
instructions: Log in as a normal user.
execution.observed_result: Static analysis only: the payload reaches cur.execute unchanged.

remediation.strategy: Use a bound parameter: cur.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)).

likelihood.reason: Any user can send the request.

impact.reason: The attacker reads every user row.

confidence.reason: The path is clear in source; no PoC ran yet.

validation_plan.local: Run the app with a test database and send the payload.

finding.reason: All three questions are established with quotes.
